audit.note: follow_up_action( control_by_id ): setP13nData on the SelectionPanel of whichever of the two p13n.Popup fragments popup_display shows (JSON arrays built in ABAP, view = POPUP); the popups' close events pass the reason and getP13nData( true ); the column drop passes the dragged/dropped p13nKey and the drop position

deviations.what: the sap.m.p13n.Engine (since UI5 1.104) is the subject of this sample. It is a JavaScript singleton, not a control - the port expresses what it does with the sap.m.p13n.Popup control (since 1.97, its close event and panels aggregation) and the sap.m.p13n.SelectionPanel control (since 1.96, its showHeader, enableCount and enableReorder properties); the app needs a UI5 release >= 1.110.

kept 1:1 from the original view and newer than 1.71: sap.m.Table autoPopinMode (1.76) and its noData aggregation holding an IllustratedMessage (aggregation 1.101, control 1.98), sap.m.Column headerMenu (1.98), the sap.m.table.columnmenu Menu control with its items aggregation and the ActionItem control with icon, label and press (all 1.110).

Engine.getInstance( ).register( ) with a Columns and a Rows SelectionController and Engine.show( ) are controller JavaScript no abap2UI5 wire can run. The port does the Engine's work in the backend: it keeps the order and visibility of the table's columns and of its five items in ABAP, and each settings button (and the column menu's Columns ActionItem) opens a p13n:Popup with one p13n:SelectionPanel (showHeader/enableCount as the SelectionController creates it, enableReorder false for Rows) - two Popup and two SelectionPanel controls the port builds as two popup_display fragments, which the original view does not have - each opened fresh on its press and destroyed (popup_destroy) in its close handler, as Engine.show( ) creates the popup per call. Right after opening one, the backend hands each panel the controller's adaptation data via setP13nData (visible entries first in state order, then the hidden ones sorted by label; labels from the two MetadataHelpers); on close with reason Ok the panel's getP13nData( true ) comes back and handleStateChange is reproduced in ABAP: every column/item hidden, the state's entries shown and moved to the front in state order. The view emits the Column and ColumnListItem controls (and every item's Text cells, which follow their column) from those two tables in a loop, so a state change is a view rebuild. The Engine's popups carry the panel's title (Fields) and contentHeight 35rem/contentWidth 32rem, which the declared Popup controls do not.

the p13n:Popup is built as a popup_display fragment of its own instead of a dependent of the table because of a UI5 leak: sap.m.p13n.Popup.addPanel moves its panels into an internal Container that only the Dialog created by open( ) takes as content, and Popup.exit destroys only that Dialog (sap/m/p13n/Popup.js, UI5 1.152) - so a Popup that is declared in a view and never opened leaks its Container and panels when the view is destroyed. abap2UI5 alternates the main view's id (mainView/mainView2) on every view_display, so two rebuilds later the leaked panels' ids collide with the new view's own and the rebuild dies on a duplicate id. A Popup that exists only while it is open (as Engine.show( ) creates it) has nothing to leak; any port that declares a p13n.Popup in a view it re-creates without opening the popup hits this. The panel ids (tableColumnsPanel/rowsPanel, invented by the port - the Engine creates its panels without one) are distinct from the other p13n fragment ports' (app 645's columnsPanel/sortPanel/groupPanel): the render gate loads every popup fragment without an id prefix into a shared page pool, where the same leak keeps a never-opened fragment's panels registered, so equal ids in two ports collided there.

onColumnMove computes the drop position from the dragged/dropped column indices and applyState( { Columns: [ { key, position } ] } ) moves the column there. The port transports both columns' p13nKey custom data and the dropPosition, does the same arithmetic on the backend's column order and moves the key in the visible-column state before re-emitting the view. The original handler searches the retrieved state with oColumn.data('p13nKey') on plain state objects, which throws as soon as the state holds a column, so in the demo kit the drop does not move anything; the port implements the move the handler evidently intends (the identical handler of sap.m.sample.p13n.Engine, which uses .key).

the sap.ui.fl VariantManagement (vm:VariantManagement p13nVm for persoTable) is dropped: variant persistence through sap.ui.fl needs a flex-enabled component with an LRep connector and the $FlexVariants model, none of which an abap2UI5 app provides, and the sap.ui.fl library is not part of the corpus' render harness. Without the Engine the control would have nothing to save.

the p13n.Popup close wires ($event.oSource.getPanels( )[0].getP13nData( true ) - read back as a JSON array of the panel's items), the setP13nData JSON argument and the drop wire's .data('p13nKey') args are source-derived, not run in a live system. **e2e-verified 2026-10-21** (nightly e2e interaction, meta/interactions/z2ui5_cl_smpc_app_649.mjs).
